papers.title: JEPA for astronomy: multi-survey spectral alignment puts stellar parameters on the leading principal axes
papers.abstract: Spectra from different surveys carry different systematics and are not calibrated against one another. Multi-survey foundation models for stellar spectra are then built by aligning embeddings of the same star observed across surveys. Most in astronomy follow the recipes established for language and vision, aligning with a contrastive loss that separates every star from the others. However, this does not ensure that the stellar physics is encoded in a form that a simple read-out can recover. Holding the cross-survey architecture fixed and varying only the alignment loss, we measure what an objective encodes from the principal-component geometry of the Gaia BP/RP (XP) spectra and from a linear probe of the stellar parameters. In a properly aligned embedding, the leading two principal components form a plane that recovers an analog of the Kiel diagram, the third component tracks [Fe/H], and [alpha/Fe] varies coherently across the plane, such that the chemically defined Galactic disks and accreted populations occupy distinct loci. We show that legibility, the ease of reading the information out, is highest for a training objective that never pushes stars apart, and instead constrains only the overall distribution of each survey's embeddings (JEPA). JEPA also exceeds the contrastive alternative at the same architecture, and the performance improves further as more surveys (Gaia XP+LAMOST LRS+DESI+APOGEE) are included. Predicted abundances for 8.0 million XP giants reproduce the main [alpha/Fe]-[Fe/H] structure of the Milky Way. These results indicate that the choice of alignment objective, not alignment alone, determines whether stellar labels are linearly recoverable.

papers.title: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
papers.abstract: With the fourth data release (DR4) from Gaia imminent, we predict neutron star (NS) binaries with luminous companions (LCs) expected to be detectable in DR4 and the final data release (DR5). We create realistic synthetic populations of NS--LC binaries in the Milky Way using COSMIC, assuming (a) observationally motivated initial distributions of binary properties, (b) metallicity and location dependent star formation history of the MW adopted from the FIRE-2 galaxy m12i, and (c) all relevant binary interaction physics, with the rapid and delayed supernova prescriptions. We estimate the detectable NS--LC population using an approximate Gaia\ selection function based on projected orbital size of the LC as well as gaiamock, which emulates Gaia's multi-epoch astrometry and orbit-fitting pipeline- both after taking into account extinction and reddening. Across supernova models and statistical fluctuations, the former (gaiamock) pipeline predicts $\sim14$--$29$ ($\sim1$--$8$), $4500$--$4700$ ($100$--$110$), and $4800$--$5000$ ($300$--$380$) detectable NS--LC binaries in DR3, DR4, and DR5, respectively. While the orbital-size based pipeline brackets the DR3 yield of NS--LC candidates, the gaiamock prediction falls short, suggesting uncertainties in the modeled binary evolution or contributions from other formation channels. DR4 is expected to directly shed light on the the relative importance of detectable NS--LC binaries from isolated binary evolution vis a vis other channels such as dynamical formation. Interestingly, our models suggest that future releases will also include $22^{+7}_{-5}\ (13^{+5}_{-4})$ and $124^{+14}_{-15}\ (53^{+10}_{-6})$ gaiamock-detectable pulsar--MS binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively, for the rapid (delayed) model, which are prime targets for radio follow-up.

papers.title: Mining the time axis with TRON. IV. MeerKAT detects a radio burst from a nearby M~dwarf
papers.abstract: We report the detection of a minute-timescale, highly circularly polarised ($\sim100\%$) radio burst from an active M dwarf (spectral type M1Ve), PM J14111$-$6155, located 19.6 pc from the Sun. Identified in the 1.28 GHz SMGPS using 8-second integrations from the TRON-pipeline, the burst peaked at 7.7 mJy. Visibility-based dynamic spectra reveal a drifting, band-limited emission feature ($\sim$300 MHz FWHM) with a maximum cut-off near 1.65 GHz, associated with electron cyclotron maser instability (ECMI), implying the existence of large-scale magnetic topologies ($B_* \approx 0.59$ kG). A non-detection ($3\sigma$ upper limit) four hours later points to intermittent or rotationally modulated beamed emission. An analysis of both TESS and ground-based survey data failed to recover an unambiguous rotational period for the optical counterpart. Follow-up SALT spectroscopy confirms its active chromospheric state, exhibiting prominent emission in the Ca {\sc ii} infrared triplet, Balmer lines, and persistent double-peaked H$\alpha$ emission ($44.6\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ peak separation) attributable to optically thick self-absorption. This discovery demonstrates that the coordinated use of time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enables direct probing of coherent radio emission from the magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs.

papers.title: Maximising the Open Magnetic Flux of a Star
papers.abstract: We consider how to distribute the magnetic flux on a star's surface in order to maximise the proportion of open magnetic flux predicted by the potential field source surface model. The proportion of open flux is shown to be maximised by concentrating all of the positive and negative flux at antipodal points. For a typical source surface height, this enhances the open flux by 35% compared to a dipolar distribution. Even if the flux is spread over finite polar caps -- as on the Sun around Solar Minimum -- the open flux is still substantially enhanced compared to the dipole. Nevertheless, we show that the dipole approximation over-estimates the open flux for this kind of flux distribution.

papers.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
papers.abstract: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars. This is theorized to happen via Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here, we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, that originates from the CEE of a ~7M$_{\odot}$ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as a ~0.7M$_{\odot}$ companion inspiraling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven year period of gradual brightening - the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core within a few (<10) orbits powers the ejection of the outermost ~10% of the stellar envelope at speeds ~10x the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope, $0.01\lesssim \alpha \lesssim 0.4$. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

papers.title: Stars and gas in the most metal-poor galaxies -- II. Search for VMS and determination of stellar population and nebular properties at $Z\lesssim0.1\,Z_\odot$
papers.abstract: Constraining the properties of OB-star populations and ionized gas at low metallicity is essential for understanding a broad range of astrophysical objects, from stellar black holes to the first galaxies. Rest-frame UV spectra of nearby metal-poor galaxies provide crucial constraints on theoretical predictions of low-metallicity stars and gas. However, such spectra are scarce at $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, and candidate Very Massive Stars (VMS) remain elusive. We analyse optical and new UV spectra of nearby star-forming galaxies with $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, selected for their nebular He II $\lambda4686$ emission and lack of Wolf-Rayet blue and red bumps, making them promising targets for VMS searches. Some galaxies exhibit stellar wind features (group 1), while others do not (group 2). For group 1, we compare STARBURST99, GALAXEV, and BPASS predictions with observed stellar lines to constrain OB-population ages and masses. The inferred ages are too old for VMS to be present. We also use pySTARBURST99 and GALAXEV photoionization models to investigate the ionized gas in a subsample, finding no evidence for VMS-dominated ionization. The absence of detected VMS may reflect their rarity, our limited sample size, or shortcomings in current models. Moreover, reproducing the extreme optical and UV line ratios simultaneously requires unrealistic N/O, ionization parameters, or Lyman continuum escape fractions, suggesting that multiple ionizing-source populations may be needed.

papers.title: Subsequent Dust-Fading Events of the Wolf-Rayet Star WR 59: A Continuous Visual Record
papers.abstract: This paper presents long-term visual and space-based monitoring of the WC9d Wolf-Rayet star WR 59 from 2017 to 2026, documenting a profound physical transition from a stable baseline to an ongoing phase of continuous dust production. Visual observations using a 22-inch telescope initially established a four-year quiescent baseline at magnitude 13.9. Following the historic May 2021 discovery fade to magnitude 15.2, long-term nightly visual monitoring documented an accelerating sequence of twelve distinct fading episodes over subsequent years, characterised by progressively shorter inter-fade recovery intervals. Due to severe pixel crowding and flux contamination from a close 11.7 V companion star 11 arcseconds away, automated large-pixel survey pipelines remain completely blind to these high-amplitude fading events. Direct comparisons with NASA's TESS satellite photometry during quiet phases show that targeted visual magnitude estimates measure systemic baseline micro-variations with professional accuracy while bridging space mission coverage gaps. High-density observation blocks during the minimum floor reveal a highly dynamic, rapid, minute-by-minute bimodal oscillation and sub-minute flickering between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2. At the time of writing, the system remains locked in an unprecedented deep minimum, varying between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2 for a sustained period exceeding 102 consecutive days. Intensive visual monitoring is ongoing to record the eventual egress recovery profile.

papers.title: Multifrequency deep radio continuum VLA observations toward OMC-2/3
papers.abstract: We present multiwavelength (0.7-5 cm) Very Large Array continuum observations of high sensitivity (3 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$), reaching an angular resolution of $0.4''$ (154 au) toward the Integral Shaped Filament in Orion. We image a field of $12.5'$ in diameter, containing the whole OMC-2 region and the southernmost $2.5'$ of OMC-3. We report the positions, flux densities and spectral indices of 47 radio sources, and discuss their nature. We conclude that, out of the 57 radio sources in the field of view, 36 (63%) are very likely tracing YSOs, 4 are tracing jet/outflow knots, and 6 are extragalactic sources; the nature of the remaining sources is unclear. We identify the driving sources of the 9 previously reported molecular outflows in our field of view. Four of them show a clear elongated radio jet morphology. We detect free-free emission from two potential photoevaporating discs associated with Class III YSOs. We find variability in 11 radio sources, 7 of which are also variable at shorter wavelengths. We find 7 pairs of radio sources with projected separations of 150-3000 au, which are potential binary systems; we identify a total of 17 potential multiple systems within this separation range when taking into account sources detected at other wavelengths. This work highlights the potential of deep VLA observations to uncover a large population of weak radio sources and study their diversity, serving as a guide for future surveys with the SKA and ngVLA.

papers.title: WFST0533buha (Bi'an): A Fast Blue Ultraluminous Transient Candidate with Unusual Blue/NUV Colors
papers.abstract: We present WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT) candidate discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope Deep High-cadence $ugr$-band Survey. The source brightened by approximately 2.5 mag in $u$ within 3 days and has a half-maximum timescale ($t_{1/2}$) shorter than 6 days. Two spectra show a blue, featureless continuum but do not provide a secure redshift. Einstein Probe observations yield only X-ray upper limits, while a faint radio counterpart was detected at 15 GHz with the VLA. The early $u$-band detection and intensive multiband coverage of Bi'an demonstrate the value of deep, high-cadence blue-band observations for discovering and characterizing FBUTs at early phases. Notably, Bi'an shows redder blue/NUV colors than AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting possible diversity in the short-wavelength properties of FBUTs.

papers.title: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
papers.abstract: Stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) originate from massive progenitors that have lost most or all of their outer envelopes prior to core collapse. Recent advances in optical time-domain surveys have revealed a growing population of peculiar SESNe with unusual light-curve morphologies, pointing to energy sources beyond the standard radioactive-decay scenario. In this work, we present multi-band photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a peculiar Type Ib supernova discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). SN 2025wiu is characterized by a high luminosity and exceptionally slow photometric evolution, with a prominent post-maximum bump peaking at $\sim50$ days after the primary maximum. Its early light curve also shows a weak excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a compact progenitor with a radius of $\sim4\,R_\odot$. The spectra show only modest evolution, with persistently weak line features and no narrow emission lines detected even at $\sim110$ days after maximum. By modeling the primary peak and late-time tail with a combination of radioactive decay and additional energy sources, we isolate the post-maximum bump, which has a roughly symmetric profile with a peak luminosity of $\sim2.4 \times 10^{42}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and a characteristic duration of $\sim42$ days. We discuss circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, accretion, magnetar activity, and a double $^{56}$Ni distribution as possible origins of the bump. The latter three scenarios face challenges in reproducing the post-maximum bump, while delayed CSM interaction remains a possible explanation.

papers.title: Sun-like stars show lowered X-ray activity together with over-rotation at beyond-solar ages
papers.abstract: In recent years, substructure in the age-rotation relationship of cool, sun-like stars has been identified, showing deviations from the historical Skumanich law. Since magnetic activity is expected to be the physical root cause of the stellar spin-down, namely via the magnetic braking process mediated through stellar winds, changes in spin-down should correspond to unusual activity behaviour. We selected a sample of old sun-like stars in the solar neighborhood with asteroseismic age estimates and measured rotation periods, and present an analysis of their magnetic activity using deep X-ray observations from XMM-Newton. We observe that sample stars less massive than the Sun (late-G and early-K) agree well with the established rotation-activity relationship, while early-G and late-F stars with masses above solar tend to be unusually X-ray dim for their rotation period. The latter stars rotate faster than same-colour stars in the solar-age open cluster M67, despite being older than M67. Those stars are characterized by either low metallicity ([Fe/H]$\approx -0.2$ dex compared to solar) or by a mix of low coronal temperatures ($< 1.5$ million K) and very low X-ray surface fluxes ($\lesssim 10^4$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$). We conclude that there is sufficient dynamo activity for coronal emission in the sample stars, since we successfully detect the majority of them in our X-ray observations. We argue that stars with extremely low coronal temperature and/or low X-ray flux through the stellar surface may produce an inefficient spin-down through hampered angular momentum shedding. If this is indeed the cause for their over-rotation, the onset age of this effect would need to be at an age of approximately 3~Gyr. However, this behaviour is at odds with studies of stars in the open cluster M67 with a cluster age of $\sim4$ Gyr, which do not show a faster-rotating population of sun-like stars.

papers.title: Welop\=o'ai: A peculiar triple system 8 pc from the Sun
papers.abstract: Context. We report the serendipitous discovery of a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) during a radial-velocity search for exoplanets with SPIRou. The system is located at 8.46 pc and forms a hierarchical triple with a more distant white dwarf, which has no known analogue within 30 pc. Aims. We characterise the orbital architecture and component masses through a joint Keplerian fit of radial velocities and astrometry, derive the physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs, and discuss the implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics. Methods. We obtained radial velocity measurements with SPIRou spread over 4.8 yr, revealing a large-amplitude signal ($\sim$16 km/s peak-to-peak) that is inconsistent with planetary companions. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and near-infrared (NIR) imaging with GNIRS confirmed a white dwarf companion at sub-arcsecond separation. Results. The system comprises an inner binary with a semi-major axis of $4.644 \pm 0.017$ au ($P \approx 9.83$ yr), consisting of the primary M4 V ($M = 0.4189^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072} M_\odot$) and a white dwarf companion ($M = 0.6180^{+0.0046}_{-0.0045} M_\odot$, $T_{\rm eff} \sim 5210 \pm 320$ K, cooling age 5.3-5.5 Gyr). This inner pair lies at a projected separation of 123.9 au ($P > 1000$ yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The dynamically determined mass of the inner white dwarf is one of only a handful of such measurements for white dwarfs within 20 pc, and the most precise, at the sub-percent (0.7%) level. Conclusions. This system is the closest known triple containing multiple white dwarfs and offers direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability. Furthermore, a tentative near-infrared (IR) excess towards the inner white dwarf further hints at circumstellar dust.

papers.title: Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with mass estimates verifiable in Gaia Data Release 4
papers.abstract: Gaia Science Alerts provide an all-sky stream of photometric transients, including events consistent with gravitational microlensing. For such events, forthcoming epoch astrometry from the Gaia mission offers the possibility of testing photometric lens mass predictions. While microlensing parallax inferred from the photometric light curve can constrain the event geometry, a direct lens mass measurement additionally requires the angular Einstein radius, which may be accessible through astrometric microlensing. We aim to construct a pre-Data-Release-4 (DR4) sample of Gaia microlensing events for which the available photometry provides a measurable microlensing-parallax signal. This allows us to derive statistical predictions for the lens mass and distance. We forward-modelled these events to predict the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal in Gaia DR4. We identify 56 Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with 71 point-source point-lens solutions with annual parallaxes that satisfy our fit-quality, posterior-boundedness, and parallax-significance criteria. Lens masses and distances were inferred using two prior-based frameworks, pyLIMASS and the Besan\c{c}on Galaxy Model, which combine the measured microlensing parameters and Gaia source information with stellar-population and Galactic models. These inferred parameters were used to simulate Gaia DR4-like along-scan astrometry and estimate the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal. The inferred lens masses and distances remain strongly prior-dependent without a direct angular Einstein radius measurement. Among the 284 event-solution-prior branches, 47 are classified as high-confidence astrometric detections using Gaia DR4-like simulations. These predictions can be tested once epoch astrometry is released in Gaia DR4.

papers.title: The infrared arc around $\alpha$ Crucis: a weak interaction with a structured interstellar medium
papers.abstract: Infrared arc-shaped structures around early-type stars are commonly interpreted as stellar wind bow shocks, although their morphology may also be shaped by gas motions and density variations in the surrounding interstellar medium. We present a multiwavelength study of the infrared arc associated with the nearby $\alpha$ Crucis system, comprising HD 108248 (B0.5 IV), HD 108249 (B1 V), and HD 108250 (B4 V). We combine WISE, Herschel, Planck, stellar astrometry, and eROSITA X-ray data to investigate the structure and its relation to the stellar components. The WISE W4 ridge extends over $\sim$0.65 pc and has a median PSF-corrected width of $\sim$0.037 pc. The HD 108248/HD 108249 pair lies $\sim$0.13 pc from the ridge, compared with $\sim$0.17 pc for HD 108250. Relative to the mean motion of the Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) subgroup of the Scorpius-Centaurus association, the close pair is consistent with LCC, whereas HD 108250 has a transverse peculiar velocity of only $\sim$1.8 km s$^{-1}$. Its motion lies within $\sim$23$^\circ$ of the geometrical symmetry axis of the infrared arc, but points in the opposite sense from the arc. Herschel maps show slightly higher median dust temperature ($\Delta T_d\sim$0.8 K) and molecular-hydrogen column density ($\Delta N_{\rm H2}\sim$7$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$) toward the W4-defined region than in the nearby background. On larger scales, Planck maps reveal a strongly structured microwave environment around the system. Both the HD 108248/HD 108249 pair and HD 108250 are detected by eROSITA, with the former approximately 60 times more luminous in X-rays. The combined morphology, kinematics, and dust properties do not support an unambiguous classical high-velocity bow-shock interpretation. Instead, the arc likely traces a weak interaction between the multiple stellar system and an inhomogeneous ambient medium.

papers.title: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
papers.abstract: We present ARTIS radiative transfer calculations for neutron star merger ejecta with line-by-line opacities, wavelength-calibrated lanthanide data, and time-dependent r-process compositions and thermalisation, testing how the early kilonova depends on the mass-velocity distribution, dimensionality, and line treatment. We rescale 3D dynamical ejecta from a merger simulation in density and velocity to approximate AT2017gfo. Mass scaling alone provides good agreement with the bolometric light curve but inconsistent spectra. With velocities additionally halved, the model also reproduces the observed spectra at 1.4, 2.4, and (albeit less accurately) 3.4 days. The Sr II triplet contributes most to the 10500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ peak, and La III and Gd III to the 13500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ shoulder. Although hydrodynamically not fully self-consistent, this model is to our knowledge the first kilonova model based on calibrated atomic data that reproduces the light curve and main spectral features of the early AT2017gfo, suggesting that total (dynamical plus post-merger) ejecta with higher mass, lower velocity, and similar composition compared to our dynamical ejecta could explain AT2017gfo. A 2D azimuthal average mixes lanthanide-poor with lanthanide-rich regions, smooths the density, and makes the averaged model three times fainter at 1 day and redder throughout than the 3D model, highlighting the importance of 3D modelling. We compare the line-by-line macroatom treatment with expansion-opacity and line-binned schemes with thermal redistribution, using identical atomic data. Luminosities agree to $\lesssim 10$ per cent after 1 day, but the expansion-opacity scheme, unlike converged line-binned schemes, overestimates the spectral flux by up to 20 per cent, which can bias inferred abundances.

papers.title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
authors: D. P. K. Banerjee (Physical Research Laboratory
M. Della Valle (Osservatorio Astronomico di Padova
G. Shaw (Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
G. Rangwal (Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Science
S. Sharma (Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Science
papers.abstract: The central star of Pa30 and its nebulosity offer one of the best opportunities to study a SN Iax explosion and its remnant. Pa30 is thought to be the product of the historical supernova explosion of 1181. No infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star has hitherto been reported. Here, we present a 0.75-5 $\mu$m spectrum taken by the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), together with ground-based infrared spectra, at higher resolution, covering the 0.8-2.5 $\mu$m region. The spectra contain very broad lines, which we have attempted to identify and model using the codes CMFGEN and CLOUDY. The CMFGEN modelling suggests that most of the lines are due to OVI. However, CLOUDY modelling, using expected theoretical abundances for the bound remnants of SN Iax explosions, provides evidence for the presence of coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from a shocked gas. This strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

papers.title: Asteroseismology of AI Velorum: a prototype of high-amplitude delta Scuti stars
papers.abstract: AI Velorum is exceptional among high-amplitude \delta Scuti (HADS) stars because of its multimode pulsations. Despite being an excellent target for asteroseismology, this prototype star has not been studied in detail. We determine the stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of AI Vel, constrain envelope convection and convective core overshooting, and test three opacity data sets: OPAL, OP, and OPLIB. We analysed TESS photometry, ground-based Str\"omgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy. Modes were identified using photometric and spectroscopic methods, and empirical values of the non-adiabatic f-parameter were derived for both radial modes. Seismic modelling was performed within a Bayesian framework supported by Monte Carlo simulations. We confirm the radial nature of the two dominant modes and identify one non-radial mode as most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Within the explored parameter space, only OPAL models reproduce the observed position of AI Vel in the HR diagram, whereas OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favour inefficient envelope convection (mixing-length parameter alpha_{mlt}\lesssim 0.5). Including the non-radial mode substantially reduces the formal posterior uncertainties, but the ambiguity in its identification introduces additional model-dependent uncertainties. AI Vel is an evolved, slowly rotating star in the hydrogen shell-burning phase. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters. The preference for OPAL opacities is consistent with results for several other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply a general superiority of OPAL opacities.

papers.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
papers.abstract: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.

papers.title: Dimming and pulsation shock of the coalesced star V838 Monocerotis
authors: C. E. Woodward (Minnesota Institute of Astrophysics)
papers.abstract: V838 Mon is the remnant of a 2002 stellar merger. Currently it closely resembles a red supergiant, but its luminosity is sustained by core H burning and continued contraction toward hydrostatic equilibrium. In late 2025, the system entered the deepest dimming event observed since 2006. We characterize the dimming event of V838 Mon using multiband photometry and high-resolution spectroscopy spanning from the dimming minimum through the recovery phase. We obtained $UBVRI JHK_s$ photometry with the NOT telescope and extracted light curves from the public AAVSO, ATLAS, ZTF, and ASAS-SN databases. These data were supplemented by time-series spectra acquired with SALT/HRS, LBT/PEPSI, VLT/Xshooter, and VLT/UVES, covering the spectral range 3760-24 800 A at resolutions $R$=6700-130 000.The photometric color evolution during the dimming can be well reproduced by grey dust extinction with $A_V$ = 1.3 mag, consistent with a transiting clump of freshly formed circumstellar dust. The photospheric effective temperature changed by no more than ~200 K during the event. During the recovery phase, H recombination lines from Balmer, Paschen, and Brackett series appeared in emission. Their line ratios do not follow Case B but are reminiscent of H emission in pulsating M-type miras near maximum light. These features are interpreted as arising from a pulsation shock propagating outward from below the photosphere. Simultaneously, low-ionization metal lines appeared blueshifted by 90 km\s relative to the stellar rest frame, tracing shock-accelerated gas on the near side of the stellar disk. The spectroscopic sequence suggests that the 2026 dimming was itself triggered by a preceding pulsation shock that occurred earlier in 2025. The observed shock may trigger a subsequent dimming event later in 2026.

papers.title: Steady-state Stellar Winds Driven by Recombination
papers.abstract: Hydrogen and helium recombination energy has been proposed as a potential driver of mass ejection in common-envelope evolution and other eruptive stellar phenomena. We investigate whether recombination can by itself launch a steady, transonic wind from near a stellar surface. Using a tabulated equation of state, we explore steady-state, adiabatic wind solutions over a broad range of stellar mass, density, and temperature. We classify a wind as recombination-driven only if the gas is gravitationally bound prior to recombination and if the released energy remains trapped until the flow becomes unbound. Only a small subset of the transonic solutions satisfies both conditions. In most cases, the gas is either already unbound without recombination or loses the released energy through radiative diffusion while still bound. The remaining candidate solutions require substantial outflow velocities of order $\gtrsim10\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ at $10\,R_\odot$ and mass-loss rates $\sim 0.1$-$10\,\rm M_\odot/yr$, which would rapidly deplete the stellar envelope. We conclude that, within our adiabatic framework and subject to an a posteriori radiative-trapping criterion, recombination energy alone is unlikely to launch a steady wind from a hydrostatic envelope. It can, however, accelerate and unbind a pre-existing outflow generated by processes such as binary orbital decay.

papers.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: A benchmark K dwarf with a compact planetary system
papers.abstract: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency. We advocate adopting the asteroseismic radius, which is robust to modeling assumptions and optimisation strategies.

papers.title: Thermodynamically consistent equation of state tables for use in giant planet and brown dwarf interior modeling
papers.abstract: Equation of state (EOS) tables used in giant planet modeling exhibit regions of strong thermodynamic inconsistency, or disobedience to the first law of thermodynamics. These generally result from smooth interpolation over physical discontinuities or between thermodynamic sub-domains governed by different physical models. The effect of thermodynamic inconsistency on structure models of planets evolved with these EOS has never been studied in detail, although it is understood to introduce spurious sources or sinks of energy or entropy in the models, leading to inaccuracies. Here, we present a method for improving the thermodynamic consistency of an existing EOS table, based on constructing a Helmholtz free energy $F(\rho,T)$ covering the EOS domain and deriving all the other necessary EOS quantities from it. This method produces EOS tables with roughly thousandfold better thermodynamic consistency across the EOS domain of interest, as quantified by three thermodynamic consistency metrics derived from the first law. We also present a controlled experiment comparing giant planet models evolved with MESA using the original EOS and the $F$-derived, thermodynamically consistent versions, and find that the models can differ by up to $5\%$ in radius at an age of 5 Gyr, and by up to $25\%$ in luminosity at earlier stages of evolution; thermodynamic consistency is thus an especially important consideration for characterising young directly imaged planets. We present the $F$-derived, thermodynamically consistent versions of the tables for download at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21103561}{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21103561}, along with example MESA inlists to reproduce our evolution models.

papers.title: Spectroscopic observations of periodic bursty ejections from a dome-spire-shaped jet
papers.abstract: Context: The study investigates the complexity of the formation and evolution of a dome-spire-shaped jet (or anemone jet) that originated in an active region and was presumably driven by null-point magnetic reconnection. Aims: We aim to provide a quantitative estimation of multi-temperature plasma dynamics and physical parameters of the jet and its blob-like features, together with its temporal evolution in three-dimensional perspective. Methods: For this, we analyze unique sit-and-stare spectral (Si IV, Mg II k, and C II) and slit-jaw imaging 1400 {\AA} and 2796 {\AA} observations obtained with the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), with a slit uniquely positioned just above the assumed reconnection site. Co-observations taken with the Fast Imaging Solar Spectrograph of the Goode Solar Telescope in the chromospheric H$\alpha$ and Ca II 8542.10 {\AA} lines were also analyzed. These data are complemented by EUV imaging information from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory. Results: The IRIS observations reveal that the jet is formed by multiple periodic ($\sim$30 s) plasma ejections with blob-like appearance, each associated with strongly blueshifted Si IV 1402.77 {\AA} transition-region emission reaching about $-300$ km/s. More importantly, the ejections are grouped into well-defined packets, each lasting approximately 3--5 min. In contrast, only a single Doppler component is observed in the chromospheric Ca II line. Multi-Gaussian decomposition of the Si IV line profiles reveals a highly accelerated plasma, with line-of-sight speed toward the observer increasing linearly from $\sim$30 to 112 km/s over 66 s, corresponding to an acceleration of 1.3 km/s$^2$. The kinetic energy release rate is estimated in the range of $\sim$1.0$\times10^{24}$--1.0$\times10^{25}$ erg\,s$^{-1}$.

papers.title: The Unusual X-ray Spectrum of R Mon
papers.abstract: The optically obscured young star R Mon illuminates Hubble's Variable Nebula and has historically been classified as an intermediate mass pre-main sequence Herbig Be star. We present Chandra observations of R Mon revealing a hard X-ray source viewed through high absorption from circumstellar gas known to be present from previous CO observations. The X-ray spectrum is characterized by line emission from the He-like Fe K complex (6.7 keV) tracing very hot plasma and fluorescent Fe emission (6.4 keV) from cold gas near the star that is irradiated by hard X-rays. Low-level variability on a timescale of less than one day is detected, but no large impulsive flares. The hot plasma and variability cannot be explained by shock models and magnetically confined plasma is inferred. The hard X-ray spectrum of R Mon does not resemble the soft spectra of prototypical Herbig stars but is remarkably similar to some class I protostars such as NGC 2071-IRS 1. As judged by its X-ray and infrared properties, we conclude that R Mon is a class I protostar and thus provides a rare snapshot of an emergent intermediate mass star enveloped in X-ray irradiated gas and dust.
